patient_information: A 33-year-old man from Finland, 180cm, 72kg (reports a 4kg weight loss), who had been backpacking in India for the previous month.
chief_complaint: Diarrhoea and flatulence for two weeks.
history_of_present_illness: The patient reported passage of loose stools (four or five episodes per day) for two weeks, along with weight loss, anorexia, malaise, flatulence, and abdominal cramping when passing stool. For the past three days, he experienced bloating and distension after milk products, with an urge to pass stool, mild nausea, but no fever. Initially, stools were watery; he took ciprofloxacin for five days, and stools became three or four per day, mushy, greasy, and foul-smelling.
exposure_and_epidemiology: He had been backpacking in India for the previous month, presenting to a private doctor in Chinglepet, Tamil Nadu.
physical_exam: Mild non-specific abdominal tenderness, no signs of dehydration; the rest of the examination was normal.
labs_and_diagnostics: Stool for reducing substances was positive. Stool examination for enteric parasites showed Giardia trophozoites in the fresh specimen and Giardia cysts on formol-ether concentrated specimens.
management_and_clinical_course: The patient was given tinidazole 2 g as a single oral dose, advised to restrict milk and high sugar products for two weeks, and counselled on food and water safety. On review after three days, his stool consistency had returned to normal, frequency decreased, nausea decreased, and anorexia decreased, although he experienced some bloating and discomfort after eating a local dessert made of reduced milk.
